terms.gloss: rivalry, the effort to equal or outdo others
terms.comment: In a good or a bad sense, as Cicero says (Tusc. 4.17); jealous rivalry is rīvālitās (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.87: ambitiō honōrumque contentiō, the competition for office

phrases.latin: ita honōris aemulātiō prō necessitāte erat
phrases.english: so competition for praise did the work of compulsion

phrases.latin: sunt etiam nōnnūllī acuendīs puerōrum ingeniīs nōn inūtilēs lūsūs, cum positīs invicem cujusque generis quaestiunculīs aemulantur
phrases.english: some games are also useful for sharpening children’s wits, when they compete by setting each other little questions of every kind

sources: Lewis & Short: aemulatio · Lewis & Short: contentio · Lewis & Short: aemulor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 44.
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 17 (concorrenza).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-tacitus, loci-quintilianus), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
